projects.name: Tarapur MIDC Industrial Area (Boisar–Tarapur)
projects.description: MIDC industrial estate at Tarapur near Boisar whose effluent is treated at the Tarapur Environment Protection Society (TEPS) CETP. Since 2016 the cluster has been the subject of National Green Tribunal proceedings over discharge of untreated effluent into creeks and the sea.

events.title: NGT orders interim compensation from defaulting Tarapur units and the TEPS CETP
events.description: In OA 64/2016 (WZ), the NGT directed defaulting non-green/white units connected to the CETP to deposit interim compensation (Rs 1 crore large, Rs 50 lakh medium, Rs 25 lakh small) and the CETP Rs 10 crore with CPCB (order dated 29.06.2019, corrected 22.10.2019), as recited in the NGT's final judgment.
events.quote: The CETP on its part shall deposit a sum of Rs. 10 Crores with the CPCB towards interim compensation within one month.

events.title: Supreme Court stays NGT interim order of 26.09.2019 (appeals by TEPS and Tarapur Industrial Manufacturers Association)
events.description: Supreme Court orders dated 18.11.2019 (Civil Appeal 8539/2019, TEPS) and 18.12.2019 (Civil Appeal 9409/2019, TIMA) stayed the NGT interim order dated 26.09.2019; NGT later held the stay covered only interim compensation, not the proceedings.
events.quote: order dated 18.12.2019 in Civil Appeal No. 9409/2019, Tarapur Industrial Manufacturers Association v. Akhil Bhartiya Mangela Samaj Parishad & Ors., staying the interim order of this Tribunal dated 26.09.2019

events.title: NGT final judgment: about 100 Tarapur units to pay ~Rs 186 crore; TEPS CETP Rs 91.79 crore; MIDC Rs 2 crore
events.description: NGT Principal Bench disposed of OA 64/2016 (WZ) filed by Akhil Bhartiya Mangela Samaj Parishad, partly allowing it; compensation to be used for environmental restoration and healthcare in the area.
events.quote: the tribunal directed the Tarapur Environment Protection Society's central effluent treatment plant to pay a compensation of Rs. 91.79 crore, and asked the MIDC to pay Rs. 2 crore.

events.title: NGT (OA 58/2024 WZ, Pasthal village pollution) constitutes Joint Committee
events.description: Suo motu proceedings on a letter petition by Anand Soman and Archana Patil about chemical effluent reaching Pasthal village drains; the Joint Committee reported in September 2024.
events.quote: this Hon'ble Tribunal vide Order dated 20.02.2024 constituted a Joint Committee

events.title: MIDC completes onshore HDPE effluent line; deep-sea disposal scheme commissioned
events.description: Per MIDC affidavit dated 12.12.2024 in OA 58/2024: 1200 mm onshore line (3.4 km) and 1000 mm offshore line (7.1 km) to an NIO-designated disposal point off Navapur.
events.quote: The entire disposal scheme i.e 1200 mm diameter 3.4 Km HDPE line onshore and 1000 mm diameter 7.1 Km HDPE line offshore is commissioned and functioning smoothly.

projects.name: Dahanu Taluka Environment Protection Authority (DTEPA)
projects.subcategory: Statutory environmental authority (EP Act s.3(3)) for ecologically fragile Dahanu taluka
projects.promoter: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
authorities: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
projects.description: Authority set up by MoEF in December 1996 on Supreme Court directions to protect ecologically fragile Dahanu taluka (declared under a 1991 notification). It rejected a Vadhavan port in 1998, and on 31 July 2023 approved JNPA's greenfield port at Vadhavan with conditions; the Bombay High Court upheld that order on 18 April 2024.

events.title: DTEPA holds a mega port at Vadhavan impermissible
events.description: On a 1997 Government of Maharashtra proposal; DTEPA treated a mega port as 'industry' under the 1991 notification. MMB's challenge (WP 7593/2003) was dismissed for want of prosecution on 23 December 2014.
events.quote: Hence, it held that construction of the Mega Port at Vadhavan was wholly impermissible.

projects.name: Palghar District Investors Summit 2026 (95 MoUs)
projects.description: District investors' summit at the Palghar Collectorate in August 2026 where 95 MoUs worth Rs 5,096.77 crore were signed (about 7,830 potential jobs). The MoUs are intentions only. Named signatories include Sky Green Recycling Industries, Aero Plast Packaging, MPCL Industries, Vstar Metal Industries and Gujarat Copper Alloys.
